wheel-angle-radians.alt: A wheel turns about an axis through its center. A painted spoke has turned counterclockwise from a dashed reference line through an angle of 1 radian: the distance along the rim between the reference line and the spoke, highlighted, equals the radius r. A curved arrow outside the rim shows the angular velocity ω, counterclockwise, called positive. A side panel pairs each straight-line quantity with its rotational partner: position x with angle θ in radians, velocity v with angular velocity ω, acceleration a with angular acceleration α, and the three constant-acceleration equations with their rotational forms. One revolution is 2π rad, or 360 degrees.
